Power Solutions International.why: Builds engine-generator power systems and enclosures for AI data centers; its power systems end market (data center products) drives its sales, so data-center power build-outs flow directly to its revenue
Power Solutions International.evidence: Power Solutions International Q2 FY2026 (08-06-2026), interim CEO/CFO Ken Li: 'Demand for our data center power solutions remains strong... we expect the second half 2026 sales to exceed the first half 2026 sales as larger power systems orders move into production'; 'our product is serving the mission-critical AI data center'

players.product: engine-generator power systems (diesel standby gensets and engines, gas gensets in development) with in-house enclosures and fuel tanks for AI data centers

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 net sales were $152.5 million, a decrease of $39.4 million, or 21%, versus Q2 2025, and up 18.6% from Q1 2026 (above the prior expectation that Q2 would be generally consistent with Q1). The year-over-year decrease was driven by $34.6 million lower sales in the power systems end markets, $3.7 million in industrial and $1.7 million in transportation; within power systems the decline primarily reflects uneven order patterns and shipment timing for data center-related products, together with continued softness in oil and gas. Interim CEO/CFO Ken Li: most of the sequential increase came from power systems, as the Wisconsin operation increased production and sales.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 net sales $152.5 million (-21% YoY, +18.6% QoQ); power systems -$34.6 million YoY

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 gross profit was $41.4 million versus $54.1 million a year earlier; gross margin was 27.1% versus 28.2% in Q2 2025 and improved approximately 420 basis points from 22.9% in Q1 2026, reflecting early benefits of operational improvement efforts in Wisconsin, partly offset by unfavorable product mix (first-half gross margin 25.2%). Net income was $16.9 million, or $0.73 per diluted share (Q2 2025: $51.2 million / $2.22, which included a $29.2 million non-recurring tax benefit). EBITDA was $25.7 million (16.9% margin) versus $34.1 million (17.8%); operating cash flow was $56.6 million; capital expenditures were $0.8 million in the quarter and $2.7 million in the first half.
quarterly_data.figure: gross margin 27.1% (Q1 22.9%, Q2 2025 28.2%); net income $16.9 million ($0.73/share); EBITDA $25.7 million (16.9%); operating cash flow $56.6 million

quarterly_data.signal: No formal full-year guidance for 2026 or 2027. Based on the current production schedule, management expects second-half 2026 sales to exceed first-half 2026 sales and to be approximately in line with second-half 2025 sales as larger power systems orders move into production and are recognized as revenue; timing and volume remain subject to customer scheduling, manufacturing flow paths and supply chain factors, and the company is 'not predicting any specific level of data center revenue in any future period'. Oil and gas softness is assumed to continue at least for this year; Wisconsin capacity ramp-up costs are expected to persist and no specific 2026 gross margin outlook is given; the longer-term goal is gross margin at or around the 25% level. More visibility on 2027 sales may be shared 'maybe in 4Q'.
quarterly_data.figure: 2H 2026 sales expected to exceed 1H 2026 and be ~in line with 2H 2025; long-term gross margin goal ~25%

quarterly_data.signal: Interim CEO/CFO Ken Li on data-center demand: 'Demand for our data center power solutions remains strong'; 'We do have some larger custom orders for the AI data center products' that the team is converting into production and sales. 'Our product is serving the mission-critical AI data center, and the capacity for the power system for the data center is constrained', with high demand for reliable, emission-certified and scalable power systems; 'we have high demand our products for 2026' and the sales team is working with customers to secure more orders for 2027. Based on customer meetings he sees strong demand for its products 'for this year and also for next year'.

Ken Li on the data-center power architecture: historically data centers used the utility grid with diesel gensets as standby; 'the trend is more towards using gas gensets for prime, then use the diesel for standby and the battery for instantaneous response'. PSI is 'also working on potentially gas gensets'. On competition, he said Weichai's Baudouin sells engine gensets to Generac while PSI sells to a different customer, so 'I don't think we are in the direct competition' (he was not sure which gensets are sold to Generac).

Wisconsin capacity: the Wisconsin footprint grew from about 150,000 square feet to about 800,000 square feet; Ken Li said current capacity can support current demand and the company can spend capital to add more capacity next year as needed. Operational initiatives improved productivity, throughput and material availability, enabling higher enclosure production and sales and better fixed-cost absorption, while capacity ramp-up costs continue to elevate production costs.
quarterly_data.figure: Wisconsin about 150,000 sq ft to about 800,000 sq ft

quarterly_data.signal: On January 9, 2026 PSI acquired MTL Manufacturing & Equipment, adding in-house manufacturing of components used in power generation products, including fuel tanks and enclosure assemblies, to enhance supply chain control and manufacturing flexibility; MTL contributed positively to Q2 consolidated net income.
